“Reinforcement learning leads to a representation of visual inputs that is more dissimilar to the other learning systems than the representations of other learning systems are dissimilar to each other.

(1) The representation of images in a deep neural network trained with reinforcement differs from those trained with unsupervised and supervised learning; (2) The representations of images in a network trained with reinforcement are more diverse than those trained with other learning objectives, as measured by a metric of neural variability; and (3) The representations of a network trained with unsupervision are more diverse than a network trained with supervision.

the representations learned by different learning systems are not interchangeable, and that the representations learned with reinforcement learning are distinct from the other representations in that they are highly flexible and diverse.

how different learning objectives influence the properties of neural network representations.

the representations learned by the different networks differ in a number of important ways, and that these differences are likely related to the differences in the learning objectives.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
reinforcement learning can be seen as the ultimate unsupervised learning problem, and as a result, reinforcement learning is a more powerful learning paradigm than unsupervised learning.
reinforcement learning is the most effective learning objective for learning representations that generalize to novel tasks and environments.
the representation learned by a network trained for reinforcement learning differs from the representations learned by supervised or unsupervised networks in a number of ways.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the objective of a learning system can have a large influence on the properties of its learned internal representations.
representations trained for different objectives have different properties, and that this should be considered when designing artificial agents.
